- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent high.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but price is trending down; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to counter mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ prices before applying sentiment-adjusted offset.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend if sentiment is negative and price is rising.
